findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the index cache without a lock while builds can write to it
findings.body:
`TotalDocs` ranges over `b.cache` without taking `cacheMu`. This PR adds a call to `s.search.TotalDocs()` in `searchSupport.init` (search.go:216). That call runs after the watch goroutine has already started (search.go:207).

The watch goroutine calls `handleEvent` → `getOrCreateIndex` → `BuildIndex`, which writes `b.cache[key]` under `cacheMu.Lock()`. Because `TotalDocs` holds no lock, a map write during its iteration is possible. That is a data race, and Go may abort the process with "concurrent map iteration and map write" during startup.

Fix: take `b.cacheMu.RLock()` in `TotalDocs`.

findings.title: Finer-grained lock allows duplicate concurrent builds of the same index
findings.body:
The lock that serialized all of `BuildIndex` is gone, and nothing deduplicates builds per key. `getOrCreateIndex` is a check-then-act sequence (`GetIndex`, then `build`), so concurrent Search requests or watch events for the same NamespacedResource can each build a full index.

Consequences:
- The last writer wins in the cache, and the other built indexes are simply discarded, wasting work.
- `IndexTenants` and `IndexedKinds` metrics are incremented more than once.
- For file-based indexes, the second `bleve.New(dir)` on the same directory fails (path exists) and the request errors.

Fix: use a per-key lock or singleflight around the build.

findings.title: Shared variables mutated from errgroup goroutines
findings.body:
Inside `group.Go`, each worker writes the outer `err` (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) and increments `totalBatchesIndexed` without synchronization. With `initWorkers > 1` these are data races.

The span attribute `namespaced_indexed` can be wrong. The returned error may also belong to a different goroutine than the one that failed.

This matters more now that the PR targets high-concurrency builds. Fix: use local variables inside the goroutine and an atomic counter.

findings.title: After Stop, RPC handlers keep serving because the Init checks were removed
findings.body:
`Stop` still sets `s.initErr` to "service is stopping" / "service is stopped". Previously every handler called `s.Init(ctx)`, which returned `initErr`, so requests were rejected after shutdown.

This PR removed those calls from every handler. `initErr` is now effectively dead after construction, and Read/List/Create/Watch keep executing against a cancelled backend and broadcaster after Stop.

Fix: either add an explicit stopped check to the handlers or remove this misleading state.

findings.title: Constructor now blocks on DB init and full index build; context leaked on failure
findings.body:
`NewResourceServer` now synchronously runs `lifecycle.Init` (DB connect/ping) and builds every search index. That makes construction slow, and it fails hard if the DB is unreachable at construction time; any caller relying on lazy init (e.g. wire/DI graphs, tests building a server without a ready DB) will break.

Also, on the error path the function returns `nil, err` without calling `cancel()`, so the cancelable context is leaked. Any goroutines started by a partial init keep running.

findings.title: Integration test disabled for postgres
findings.body: The storage-server integration test is now skipped on postgres, with only a TODO and no linked issue. Since this PR changes startup behaviour (init in the constructor), this loses coverage exactly where regressions are likely. It may also be hiding a real startup failure introduced by this change.
